Synopsis:
    CCW member states met in Geneva to decide on a non-binding text that could open negotiations on regulating Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS). The process is at risk of failure due to last-minute US and Russian opposition, with Washington pushing for flexible guidelines over binding treaty language. Key sticking points include human control provisions and specific terminology. A broader coalition including Brazil, Ireland and African states supports binding rules. No deal would leave autonomous weapons — increasingly deployed in active conflict zones — without dedicated international legal standards.
